title: Braaied Peri-Peri Chicken
author: Chef Manuel
desc: A chicken spatchcocked flat, basted with half a batch of peri-peri and turned every five minutes over medium coals for forty-five minutes — with the other half of the sauce finished in coconut milk as a dip.
longDesc: Flattening the bird is the whole method: spatchcocked, it cooks evenly and it gets maximum surface against the coals, which is where the sauce caramelises. The discipline is in the heat and the turning — medium coals and a turn every five minutes, because a sauce with this much sugar and pepper in it burns on high heat long before the chicken is done. Half the sauce goes on raw chicken; the other half becomes the dip, which keeps it safe.
ingredients: 8 to 10 bird's-eye or serrano chillies, chopped
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
equipment: Sharp scissors or a heavy knife, to spatchcock
steps: Braai the onion and pepper halves and the halved head of garlic over medium coals, turning every 5 minutes, for about 15 minutes until softened and charred at the edges.
Let them cool slightly, then blend with the chillies, smoked paprika, olive oil, vinegar, lemon zest and juice until smooth. Season.
Simmer the sauce in a saucepan for 5 minutes.
Baste the spatchcocked chicken with half the sauce and braai it over medium coals for 45 minutes, turning every 5 minutes, until cooked through.
Add the coconut milk to the remaining sauce and simmer for 5 minutes to make the dip.
Serve the chicken with the dipping sauce alongside.
chefTips: Medium coals and a turn every five minutes. High heat burns the sauce black while the thigh is still raw at the bone, and that is the only real way to ruin this.
Spatchcock it properly — cut out the backbone and press the bird flat. A whole round chicken will not cook evenly on a grid.
Half the sauce for basting, half for the table. Never serve back sauce that has been brushed onto raw chicken.
Blistering the vegetables on the coals rather than in the oven gives the sauce its smoke, which is worth the extra fifteen minutes.
The thigh should read 75C at the bone. Forty-five minutes is a guide and birds vary.
commonMistakes: Cooking it over hot coals, which chars the baste and leaves the meat underdone.
Basting with the whole batch of sauce.
Leaving it undisturbed on the grid, so one side blackens.
Skipping the coconut milk in the dip — it is what takes the edge off enough to dunk.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. The dip keeps 4 days.
reheating: Warm in a moderate oven, covered. The skin will not re-crisp fully.
healthBenefits: Chicken provides lean protein, niacin and selenium.
Grilled over coals, so most of the fat renders away.
The sauce is built on roasted vegetables rather than oil or cream.
culturalNote: Flame-grilled peri-peri chicken is one of the very few dishes that reaches nearly every South African through a restaurant chain as well as a home kitchen. The chain version is a descendant of the Portuguese-Mozambican original rather than the source of it, and the difference shows most in the smoke.
